full_query: A 27-year-old man presents for an appointment to establish care. He recently was released from prison. He has felt very fatigued and has had a cough. He has lost roughly 15 pounds over the past 3 weeks. He attributes this to intravenous drug use in prison. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. QuantiFERON gold testing is positive. The patient is started on appropriate treatment. Which of the following is the most likely indication to discontinue this patient's treatment? (A) Elevated liver enzymes (B) Hyperuricemia (C) Optic neuritis (D) Peripheral neuropathy (E) Red body excretions

B) Hyperuricemia: Hyperuricemia (high levels of uric acid in the blood) can be a side effect of certain medications used to treat TB, such as rifampicin

C) Optic neuritis: Optic neuritis is an inflammation of the optic nerve and can be a side effect of some medications used to treat TB, such as isoniazid
However, it is a rare side effect and not typically an indication to discontinue treatment
D) Peripheral neuropathy: Peripheral neuropathy is a well-known side effect of isoniazid, a medication commonly used to treat latent TB
It can occur at any time during treatment, and if it occurs, the treatment is often discontinued
E) Red body excretions: Red body excretions are not a known side effect of TB treatment
Based on the information provided, the most likely indication to discontinue this patient's treatment is peripheral neuropathy, due to the common association with isoniazid
